GJT.name: Grand Junction
GJT.excerpt: The next chance for impactful weather comes mid to late next week beginning Tuesday as a low pressure system dives down the west coast and forms a deep closed low over the Desert Southwest.
GJT.text:
As the trough moves further east over the Midwest, high pressure builds behind over the Great Basin and Intermountain West forming a Rex Block heading into Friday with northerly flow over the region. Much colder air mass settles over the region tonight with lows in the 20s for the northwest Colorado valleys (Yampa River Basin) where a widespread hard freeze appears likely. Other areas in a Freeze Warning tonight include the upper Colorado River valley (COZ008) from Glenwood to Avon and the San Juan River Basin (COZ023). A Freeze Warning remains in effect for those same areas Friday night as well, so depending on how widespread of a hard freeze occurs in these zones would determine whether additional freeze warnings are needed. Outside of these areas, temperatures will be cooler but not expecting temperatures below freezing for the overnight.

High pressure moves overhead by Saturday as the Rex Block breaks down and the low that was at the bottom of the Rex Block will open up and pull enough moisture with it to bring isolated showers to the San Juans as it tracks over the Four Corners Sunday afternoon. This is fairly weak so not expecting much impact but drier conditions overall this weekend with temperatures around 5 degrees or so below seasonable. Isolated showers are possible again over the high terrain Monday afternoon as southwest flow keeps the area a bit unsettled. Temperatures overall will bump up a little bit towards normal but lean on the side of below seasonable for most areas.

BOU.name: Boulder / Denver
BOU.excerpt: Currently, both the GFS and ECMWF deterministic solutions bring in our next trough Thursday or Friday. This far out, though, the timing of this system is highly uncertain, as is the location of the cutoff low/trough axis.
BOU.text:
Recent obs show temperatures starting to drop over parts of the eastern plains, and most of the cloud cover from earlier today has cleared out. A Freeze Warning remains in effect until 9am Friday for the eastern plains & I-25 corridor, where lows tonight are expected to drop into the upper 20s-low 30s. Winds should stay light across the area overnight, with some breezier conditions (gusts of about 15- 20mph) in the northeasternmost plains.

Cooler temperatures persist Friday, with highs in the mid to upper 50s across the plains & I-25 corridor. Downsloping winds should keep lows tomorrow night above freezing for most of the foothills, while the northern and easternmost plains should again see lows in the upper 20s-low 30s. Despite the good model agreement in below freezing temperatures across the plains Friday night, we have decided to hold off for now on issuing any frost or freeze products until we know tonight's low temperatures. Should a killing freeze hit tonight (low temps <= 28F), we would not issue another product; however, if lows don't quite reach that 28 degrees or less threshold, we may be looking at another frost/freeze product.

Temperatures warm back up on Saturday as a ridge moves into the area. Highs are expected to be in the upper 70s on Saturday as the ridge axis moves across the state, with southwest flow dominating on the upstream side of the ridge by Sunday, keeping temps on the warmer side through the first half of next week and pulling in some mid-level moisture. While conditions should stay dry over the plains and urban corridor, we can't rule out a few afternoon rain/snow showers over the higher terrain Sunday through Wednesday.

Currently, both the GFS and ECMWF deterministic solutions bring in our next trough Thursday or Friday. This far out, though, the timing of this system is highly uncertain, as is the location of the cutoff low/trough axis. PUB.name: Pueblo
PUB.excerpt: Upper low will translate through the western U.S. towards CO into late week, though details on timing, track and strength are highly variable at this point.
PUB.text:
Warmer conditions return over the weekend with ridging aloft transitioning to southwest flow ahead of a filling upper low entering southern CA and western AZ on Sunday. Saturday remains dry across southern CO but some moisture advects in for Sunday and Monday as this weakening upper level disturbance gradually lifts out across CO. Some isolated showers will be possible, mainly for the mountain areas with some spotty light rainfall possible. Snow levels will remain above 10000 feet during the day time hours when showers will be most prevalent.

The next upper trough moves into the west coast Tuesday and Wednesday. This will increase southwest flow over CO bringing breezy and warm conditions with increasing showers across the Continental Divide. Best chances for showers will be across the eastern San Juans due to orographically favored southwest flow, however this will be warm system with snow levels remaining high.

Upper low will translate through the western U.S. towards CO into late week, though details on timing, track and strength are highly variable at this point. Trend will be towards unsettled weather and a cool down perhaps next weekend as the system crosses the Rockies.

CYS.name: Cheyenne
CYS.excerpt: The long term will be mostly controlled by high pressure ridging, though several embedded disturbances will help to disrupt this feature from growing stronger and brining much warmer conditions, while modest moisture should bring at least a weak chance of precipitation through this period.
CYS.text: The long term will be mostly controlled by high pressure ridging, though several embedded disturbances will help to disrupt this feature from growing stronger and brining much warmer conditions, while modest moisture should bring at least a weak chance of precipitation through this period. The long term starts with upper level high pressure controlling much of the southeastern US and extending up towards our region, while a weak low off of the southwestern California coastline moves inland and up towards the Four Corners region while continuing to weaken. This system, while weak and mostly non-impactful, will at least help to stave off the ridge from strengthening over the region while also bringing a quick and weak shot of moisture that should fuel a few weak upper elevation showers in the region. We will be clearing out on Monday again before flow turns more southerly to southwesterly on Tuesday as a deep Pacific low begins to approach the west coast and then moves inland through the end of the forecast period. This will continue to stream moisture in, allowing for further increasing chances of upslope induced precipitation that will be aided by embedded weak shortwaves within the flow, though once again not expecting significant accumulations from this activity. Under this pattern look for temperatures to remain largely the same through the long term as highs sit generally 5-10 degrees above normal (60's to upper 70's), with portions of eastern Wyoming and the Nebraska Panhandle nearing 80 degrees, but currently not expected to reach this warm. Otherwise, with no significant features present over our area, look for largely benign conditions until likely just beyond the long term into the weekend after next. SLC.name: Salt Lake City
SLC.excerpt: The previously mentioned upper level trough will be off the central California Coast by Tuesday morning.
SLC.text:
A warming trend will continue as high pressure remains overhead through the first part of the weekend. A cut off upper level low currently over southern California will continue to retrograde westward. Meanwhile, the continued very active eastern Pacific will have at least two ongoing tropical cyclones (Simon and Trudy). As the upper level low continues to shift westward, tropical moisture from weakening Tropical Storm Simon will be drawn northward into Baja California and eventually the Desert Southwest Sunday.

This upper level low will eject across the Desert Southwest ahead of the next Pacific trough Sunday. PW anomalies from this moisture advection ahead of the low will reach near 90-95th percentile across southern Utah. While it is mid-October, if sufficient destabilization occurs, a few thunderstorms capable of heavy rain will develop Sunday afternoon and evening across southern Utah. This threat will continue Monday afternoon and evening.

The previously mentioned upper level trough will be off the central California Coast by Tuesday morning. Broad upper level divergence ahead of this upper level trough combined with PVA will support the develop of widespread precipitation across central and southern Utah by Tuesday afternoon. As this trough slowly crosses the West, additional periods of valley rain and high elevation snow will continue through at least the early weekend period. Rainfall totals (25th to 75th percentile) are averaging around 0.50 to 1.50 inches across most locations, with some areas that do well in southerly flow (northern Wasatch Front, Provo Canyon, southern mountains) likely seeing more than 2 inches. As far as snow, while it's over several days, looking like another 6 to 12 inches, mainly above 9000-9500 feet.

Going Freeze Warnings are on track and no changes will be made. No additional headlines are needed at this juncture.

BOI.name: Boise
BOI.excerpt: Temperatures will remain about 5 to 10 degrees above normal on Monday, however the pattern change will be actively underway. Through the rest of the week, a high amplitude trough will become a cut off low in southern California and linger in the Great Basin.
BOI.text: Temperatures will remain about 5 to 10 degrees above normal on Monday, however the pattern change will be actively underway. Through the rest of the week, a high amplitude trough will become a cut off low in southern California and linger in the Great Basin. As the trough builds along the West Coast Monday evening, increasing clouds and breezy conditions in SE Oregon are expected. Temperatures will cool off Tuesday as a front move through, cooling temperatures down to near-normal; low-mid 60s for the afternoon high in lower elevations, low 50s for mountain valleys. The cloud cover and increasing chance of precipitation Tuesday evening through Thursday evening could help to moderate temperatures further, however precipitation confidence at this time is low.
